name: thetaLarge_move
summary: Landherr's theorem moves V₁ to V (c′, k′); the theta integrals are integrals over the same orbit, the theta functionals compared through the vacuum and products of line thetas; the constant is a character value of det k/det k′.

steps.claim: By Landherr's theorem (`Space.exists_eq_move`) V and V₁ differ by a rational change of coordinates c′ and a point k′ (w: the Gram relation); and the datum of Hom(W, V) maps rational vectors to rational vectors (`Space.exists_mapsTo_ratVectors`; a, q).
steps.lean: obtain ⟨⟨c', k', w, _⟩, a, q⟩ := V₁.exists_eq_move V, (W.hom V).exists_mapsTo_ratVectors

steps.claim: Take u = rankTwist(ν_𝔠⁻¹, n)(det k/det k′); it remains, for each v, Φ, g, to compare the two theta integrals (unfolding thetaLarge, thetaIntegral, localDatum and name).
steps.lean:
use (rankTwist 𝔠.ν⁻¹ n).1 (k.det / k'.det), fun f Φ g ↦
    .symm ?_; delta thetaLarge thetaIntegral localDatum name

steps.claim: Change variables in the integral over [U(V)] by conjugation with k′ (`identDistrib_orbitMeasure_comp`: counting measure on the rational points, left multiplication by k′, rationality of theta) and move the constant into the integral.
steps.lean:
rw [← (identDistrib_orbitMeasure_comp (H := V.Γ) (measurePreserving_count
    ((MulAut.conj k').subtypeEquiv (by simp [Γ, reindex_equiv (U.conj _ w), *])))
    (measurePreserving_mul_left _ k') (by simp [Subgroup.smul_def, mul_assoc])
    ((pairThetaKer ..).swap.theta_rat_mul _ ·.2)).integral_eq, ← integral_const_mul]

steps.claim: Compare the integrands: the products of points and the Weil actions.

The theta functional of the moved datum equals that of the original datum, both being products of line thetas of the vacuum translates (`ext_of_vacElem`, `theta_vacElem_eq_prod_lineTheta`), provided the moved coordinates map rational vectors to rational vectors (left open).
steps.lean:
rw [← ext_of_vacElem _ a (T := (W₁.hom V₁).θ ∘L ω _ (onHom (k, k'))) fun z ↦
    (congrArg _ (rep_apply_apply ..)).trans ((theta_vacElem_eq_prod_lineTheta (fun y h ↦ ?_)
    z).trans (theta_vacElem_eq_prod_lineTheta q z).symm)]

steps.claim: Rewrite the rationality condition through the matrix action on vectors.
The rational vectors are preserved: y ↦ c′·y·c⁻¹ maps rational vectors of Hom(W₁, V₁) to those of Hom(W, V) (from q and hk).
steps.lean:
exact (mem_ratVectors_hom.1 (q y h)).imp' (c'.1 * · * c⁻¹.1) (by simp_all [mat,
               ← (c'.map _).1.mul_assoc, ← GeneralLinearGroup.val_map_apply, -coe_units_inv])
